gen-dafont-junegull-gf-comme: Comme reads smooth and modern, its lowercase filling most of the letter height. Junegull's pinched curve mouths and cast-iron stature give it a retro, friendly weight that the open body lets stand out.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-cossette-texte: Chunky, retro and a bit cheeky up top, with Junegull's curves pinched nearly shut; below, Cossette Texte opens wide with a prominent x-height. It reads steadily, with no snags.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-duru-sans: Pinched and playful, Junegull holds the top with its engraver-cut strokes of single depth. And Duru Sans sits beneath with wide-open small letters whose bodies dominate each line, so the two feel like opposites sharing a page.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-fresca: Friendly retro punch, courtesy of Junegull's pinched curves and tall cast-iron lowercase. Fresca follows with big bowls, short ascenders and counters kept open to the outside, which loosens everything the heading squeezes shut.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-funnel-sans: Funnel Sans keeps its lines tidy and its e pried wide open. Next to Junegull's pinched, closed-up retro curves, it feels like a deep breath after a snug hug.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-gafata: Gafata stacks a tall band of lowercase under short stalks, and its wide-eyed e keeps each word easy to pick out. Over a full page it moves along quickly.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-geist: Junegull brings a retro, friendly look with pinched curve mouths and lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals, while Geist stays quiet below it. The strongest quality is how snug closed letters meet open ones.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-georama: Georama's wide-open c looks like a bracelet pulled apart, and its capitals barely rise above the lowercase. Down a long page it feels relaxed.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-gidole: Junegull leads with a retro, friendly swagger, its curves pinched and its strokes cut to one depth. But Gidole answers in open, neon-tube lines with a high midline, and that gap keeps the page lively.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-golos-text: Golos Text fills the line with a large x-height and a widely parted s, drawn in one width of stroke. But Junegull does the showy work, with pinched curves and cast-iron lowercase that body text never attempts.
